name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)
strategy: Rate-cycle rotation + carry + early trend-reversal with stop discipline: energy as the oil/Hormuz hedge, value, a reduced large-cap financials stake after bank earnings, unhedged Japan, income carry, healthcare, a long-Treasury trend-reversal leg against a 10-year that has backed off its 10-07 peak, with the two failed crypto trend legs cut and 33% cash at 4% into the 10-27/28 Fed meeting.
reassessment_note: Research done with WebSearch/WebFetch on 2026-10-17. The book is doing its job: +6.17% vs SPY +2.94% with a -2.08% max drawdown, and this week's rotation out of tech into Dow/value/financials/energy is exactly what it was built for (Dow +0.7-1.5% on the week while Nasdaq fell 4.5%). The macro confirms the thesis rather than challenging it: September CPI 3.7% / core 2.6% (hot), ~94% December-hike odds, Fed meeting 10-27/28, Brent touched $110 on Iran's escalating Hormuz attacks, 10-year ~5.07-5.10% and 30-year ~5.42% but both retreating from the 10-07 intraday peak (30-year fell 10bp on 10-16 even with the hot CPI, which supports the TLT trend-reversal leg). Bank earnings were solid (JPM $5.57 EPS, revenue $50.2B, 2026 NII guide raised to $106.2B; Visa/Mastercard at records; Truist a miss), so XLF stays at its reduced 7%. XLE is +7.55% on the leg and is the hedge for the thing most likely to go wrong (oil). EWJ's -4.45% is the unhedged yen (~158 on 10-08) plus the semi-heavy Nikkei's pullback from ~70,000; the yen near the level where the US and Japan intervened in August makes unhedged exposure a reasonable asymmetric bet, so it stays with its 12% stop. JEPQ's -3.9% is Nasdaq beta; higher VIX (22) raises the covered-call income, so the carry leg stays. The one change: I cut ETH (-10.7%) and SOL (-13.6%). They were entered on 10-05 as 'early trend-reversal' legs and the reversal has not come - BTC is 36% off its high, ETF outflows continue, ~$1B of leveraged longs were liquidated on the CPI day, and a Fed hike cycle resuming is the wrong regime for long crypto beta. Stop discipline means cutting a failed trend trade at -11/-14% rather than waiting for the -22/-25% stop to do it; the exit costs ~3bps of NAV. The freed 8% goes to cash at 4% (33% total) rather than chasing XLE after a +7.5% move or adding gold at $4,181 unresearched. Every equity leg keeps its prior weight and stop percentage; re-basing the stops to the 10-19 fill tightens the absolute protection on the winners (XLE, XLV, TLT, IWD, XLF). Novelty check vs my Round 2 book (NVDA/MU/AMD/TSM/ANET/BTC): zero same-direction symbol overlap. Risks accepted: a surprise October hike would hurt TLT (7% stop bounds it), a Hormuz ceasefire would gap XLE down (12% stop), and a sharper US slowdown would hit XLF and IWD.

positions.thesis: The oil/Hormuz hedge, +7.55% on the 10-05 leg with Brent touching $110 (first time since May) on Iran's escalating strait attacks and WTI ~$98-100. Kept at 12% rather than added to because a ceasefire or sanctions-easing headline would gap it down; the 12% stop re-based to the 10-19 fill now protects most of the gain.

Large-cap value is the direct beneficiary of this week's rotation out of tech (Dow up on the week while Nasdaq fell 4.5%, SOXX down nine sessions). In a resuming hike cycle with a 5%+ 10-year, value's shorter duration is the right factor. Unchanged at 12% with a 12% stop.

Reduced financials stake carried through bank earnings: JPM beat ($5.57 EPS, $50.2B revenue) and raised 2026 NII guidance to $106.2B, Goldman $18.7B revenue, Visa/Mastercard at record highs, Truist a miss. A steeper curve and higher-for-longer rates help NII; kept at the reduced 7% because trading/IB fees were softer and a growth scare would hit credit. 10% stop.

Unhedged Japan: the -4.45% on the leg is mostly yen weakness (~158/USD on 10-08, back near the August US-Japan intervention zone) plus the semi-heavy Nikkei's pullback from ~70,000. BOJ at 1.0% with 1.25% expected later in 2026 and Japan manufacturing output at a 12-year high on AI orders; yen intervention risk is upside for an unhedged holder. Unchanged at 10% with a 12% stop.

Income carry leg on the Nasdaq-100: -3.9% is index beta from the tech selloff, but VIX at 22 raises the covered-call premium this fund sells, so the carry improves exactly when the index is weak. Keeps a controlled slice of tech exposure in a book otherwise rotated away from it. Unchanged at 10% with a 10% stop.

Defensive healthcare, +5.58% on the leg, working as the low-beta diversifier while tech sold off (Moderna's -9% on 10-16 was a single-name reversal after a 600% run, not a sector signal). Unchanged at 8% with a 12% stop re-based to the 10-19 fill.

Long-Treasury trend-reversal leg, +3.81% on the 10-05 entry. The 10-year (~5.07-5.10%) and 30-year (~5.42%) are both ~25-30bp below the 10-07 intraday peak, and the long end rallied 10bp on 10-16 despite the hot CPI, which is the growth-scare/flight-to-quality behaviour the leg was built for. A December hike is already ~94% priced. Tight 7% stop keeps it honest if the 10-07 high in yields is retested; unchanged at 8%.
